acceptance_criteria.criterion: Clicking "Auto-Setup Tools" in Settings opens the `SetupWizard` as a modal using the existing `BlockingModal` pattern.
The wizard shows a progress bar and current step message, updated in real-time via `setup-progress` Tauri events.
On successful installation, `phpPath` and `installPath` in the app config are updated automatically via `ConfigContext.updateConfig`.
On error, an error message is displayed with a retry button that re-invokes `download_and_install_tools`.
The "Auto-Setup Tools" button is only visible when `config.phpPath` or `config.installPath` is empty or invalid.
All new user-facing strings use `t()` from `I18nContext` — no literal strings in JSX.
All setup wizard strings appear correctly in English; German and French show placeholder translations.
No TypeScript errors in modified files.

summary: Created SetupWizard.tsx: modal overlay component with real-time setup-progress event subscription, animated progress bar, error display with retry, and optional Check for Updates panel.

Updated SettingsView.tsx: added relative positioning, showSetupWizard state, needsSetup computed flag, handleWizardComplete callback, Auto-Setup Tools button (Wand2 icon) in Environment & Tools header — button only visible when installPath empty or phpPath is default.
Added setup.* i18n strings to en.json (full English), de.json, and fr.json (native placeholder translations).
Updated data-flows.md with full Installation Wizard Flow section, file-tree.md with SetupWizard.tsx entry, and detail-screens.md with Section 5 documenting the wizard's props, state, and behaviour.
TypeScript: no errors. Vitest: 7/7 tests pass, no regressions.

comments.note: SettingsView.tsx has several hardcoded English strings in JSX (e.g. 'Environment & Tools', 'Debugging', 'Web Server', 'Appearance', 'Browse') that bypass the i18n system. These are pre-existing and out of scope for WP-004, but should be addressed in a future i18n cleanup pass.

BlockingModal.tsx is a very thin wrapper around a fixed layout and content (lock icon + invalid_config/modal_message strings). Generalising it into a reusable ModalOverlay primitive would allow SetupWizard and future modals to share the backdrop/animation without duplicating the absolute-overlay pattern.

The SetupProgress and InstalledPaths types are defined in SetupWizard.tsx as exports. If additional Tauri command types grow, a shared src/types/tauri.ts file would centralise them consistently with how the rest of the codebase imports from context files.

summary: TypeScript: clean (tsc --noEmit exit 0). Vitest: 7/7 tests pass, 0 regressions across 3 test files.

AC1 (BlockingModal pattern): SetupWizard.tsx uses identical overlay classes to BlockingModal.tsx (`absolute inset-0 z-10 flex items-center justify-center p-6 bg-white/60 dark:bg-gray-950/60 backdrop-blur-[2px] rounded-3xl animate-in fade-in duration-300`). Pattern fully replicated.
AC2 (setup-progress events): `listen<SetupProgress>('setup-progress', ...)` subscribes on mount; `progress.message` and `progress.percent` drive the progress bar and step text.
AC3 (config update): SettingsView.handleWizardComplete calls `updateConfig({ phpPath: paths.php_path, installPath: paths.install_path })` via ConfigContext.
AC4 (error + retry): Error state renders error text from catch block and a Retry button that calls `startInstallation` directly.
AC5 (button visibility): `needsSetup = !config.installPath || !config.phpPath || config.phpPath === 'php'` — covers empty, null, and default-unset phpPath.
AC6 (i18n): All JSX strings in SetupWizard.tsx go through `t()`. String interpolation for {version} uses `.replace()` on the translated string — AC letter met.
AC7 (locales): All three locale files (en.json, de.json, fr.json) contain the full `setup.*` key set (11 keys each). German and French are fully translated.

metrics.test_coverage: 7/7 existing tests pass; SetupWizard.tsx has no dedicated unit tests

comments.note: SetupWizard.tsx useEffect on mount calls startInstallation() but returns no cleanup. If the component unmounts while the Tauri invoke is in-flight (parent forced close), state updates run on an unmounted component. In practice the close button is hidden during isRunning so this path is blocked by UI.

SetupWizard.tsx has no unit tests. Mocking @tauri-apps/api/core and @tauri-apps/api/event is already set up in src/test/setup.ts, so adding a basic smoke test (renders header, starts install on mount) would be straightforward.

setup.update_available and setup.up_to_date strings use t(key).replace('{version}', ...) instead of native i18n interpolation. This works but is inconsistent if the I18nContext ever gains built-in interpolation support.

summary: Reviewed SetupWizard.tsx, SettingsView.tsx, all three locale files, and setup.rs against WP-004 acceptance criteria. All 8 AC met. Architecture is clean and consistent with existing patterns.

SetupWizard.tsx: Correct overlay class reuse from BlockingModal pattern (AC1). setup-progress event listener with proper unlisten() in finally block (AC2). handleWizardComplete calls updateConfig before closing modal (AC3). Error state with Retry button re-invokes startInstallation (AC4). needsSetup covers empty, null, and default-'php' phpPath (AC5). All JSX strings go through t() (AC6). All 11 setup.* keys present in en/de/fr locales (AC7). TypeScript clean (AC8).

Rust setup.rs (WP-002): zip-slip protection via enclosed_name() is correct. Streaming download avoids memory bloat. Windows-only guard returns clear error without panic. HTTPS used for PHP download URL.

One medium finding: checkForUpdates catch block sets updateInfo to { latest_version: '', update_available: false } which causes the UI to render 'You are up to date ()' with an empty version string when the GitHub API is unreachable — misleading. Recommend setting updateInfo to null (or a distinct error state) in the catch block instead.
Pre-existing hardcoded English strings in SettingsView.tsx (Appearance, Debugging, Web Server) are correctly out of scope for this WP.

comments.note: SetupWizard.tsx checkForUpdates catch block (line ~67) sets updateInfo to { current_version: null, latest_version: '', update_available: false } on failure. This renders the update badge with an empty version string ('You are up to date ()'), which is misleading. Recommend setting updateInfo to null in the catch block so no badge is shown when the check fails, or introducing a dedicated error state for the update check panel.

setup.rs: setup-progress event message strings are English literals embedded in Rust (e.g. 'Fetching latest release info...', 'PHP download complete.'). These cannot pass through the frontend i18n system. Acceptable for an internal progress signal, but users will see English-only progress messages regardless of locale selection. Future improvement: use step codes on the frontend side for i18n-mapped messages.

SetupWizard.tsx useEffect dependency array suppression (eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps) is intentional — mount-only invocation — but bypasses linting. Using a useRef guard (hasRun.current) would achieve the same intent without silencing the linter.

summary: Fixed Reviewer medium finding: SetupWizard.tsx checkForUpdates catch block now sets updateInfo = null (was a fake success object with empty latest_version), preventing misleading 'You are up to date ()' badge on network failure.
